references.supports: Debiased NEO orbital and absolute-magnitude distributions and source-region priors.
references.does_not_support: The exact production ordering score or discovery probability.

references.supports: ZTF twilight searches for interior-Earth objects at solar elongations down to about 35 degrees.
references.does_not_support: The selector's exact preference peak, eligibility bounds, or expected yield.

references.supports: Population-completeness estimation using discovery and re-detection statistics.
references.does_not_support: The production ordering score or absolute candidate quality.

empirical_evidence.supports: Promotion of geometry-only ordering over the former weighted policy and a regularized three-feature alternative, including the small available 2024 Aten holdout.
empirical_evidence.does_not_support: A calibrated probability, causal yield, adequately powered IEO holdout, or globally optimal ranking rule.

empirical_evidence.supports: Geometry is the strongest available single-component ordering for both source-aligned Aten and IEO outcome sets and materially exceeds the former weighted policy on the same recorded outcomes.
empirical_evidence.does_not_support: A calibrated probability, causal yield, external holdout performance, or globally optimal coefficients.

empirical_evidence.supports: The direction of the class-specific geometry revision using real source-aligned discovery observations.
empirical_evidence.does_not_support: A precise optimum or an independent external validation sample.

limitations: This is a deterministic ordering score, not a calibrated discovery probability.
The geometry preference peaks and component comparison use overlapping retrospective outcomes and may be optimistic.
The source-aligned ieo sample is small at 7 positive and 7 searched-null records.
Absolute quality is reported separately; no score threshold suppresses top-N selection.
New-target history and exact executability are hard eligibility gates, not soft ranking coefficients.
